Does the offer seem OVERWHELMING? If so, how can you tweak it?
How can you set your offer stack as a timeline? How soon can you get them the result?
Have you made sure there does NOT seem to be any problem introduced by the final element of your offer?
concepts: Two Ingredients To Make Your Offer Irresistible: (1) Solve One Problem + Create A New One, (2) Tie Your Offer To A Timeline
Offer Stack Chain: each component solves the new problem introduced by the previous component (traffic -> funnel -> software -> course -> copywriting, etc.)
Feel Complete: your customers should feel like you are giving them ALL the tools to make them successful
Tie to a Timeline: build the offer stack as a timeline so buyers can project themselves into the future having the result they want
Timeline example: 'Here is how to get six-pack abs in six weeks' / week-by-week build of offer results
Overwhelm-to-Achievable pivot: tying the offer to a timeline makes an overwhelming stack feel achievable step-by-step
ROI framing: buyers need to feel they can get a return on their investment in X weeks, not some vague time in the future
Final element rule: the last element in the stack must NOT introduce a new problem

STEP 2: Answer whether the offer seems COMPLETE — and how to tweak it if not

STEP 3: Fill out the Timeline table for Elements 1-8, mapping each element to a timeline
Reflection: verify the final element does not introduce a new problem

questions: What are the 3 Core False Beliefs your audience holds that you must address for your Big Domino to take everything else down with it?
What is the Vehicle belief — the false belief that your New Opportunity won't work in general?
What are the Internal Beliefs — the false beliefs they hold about themselves that they cannot succeed using your New Opportunity?
What are the External Beliefs — the false beliefs that external factors (outside them) will make it impossible somehow?
What is the headline for your first secret (addressing your Vehicle)?
What is the headline for your second secret (addressing their Internal Beliefs)?
What is the headline for your third secret (addressing their External Beliefs)?
Does it have to be exactly 3 Secrets, or could it be 3 Myths, 3 Lies, 3 Questions, etc.?
concepts: The 3 Secrets = the variety of different angles used to emphasize the single point of belief (Big Domino) over and over
Flexible format: doesn't have to literally be 3 Secrets — could be 3 Myths, 3 Lies, 3 Questions, etc.
Single Point of Belief principle (Jason Fladlien): one core belief emphasized from many different angles

The 3 Core False Beliefs framework: (1) The Vehicle — your New Opportunity itself; (2) Internal Beliefs — what they believe about themselves; (3) External Beliefs — what they believe about external factors
Vehicle belief: 'Your New Opportunity itself may convince some people in the room, but maybe not all of them.' You must prove the vehicle works.
Internal belief handling: convince them that they themselves can have success using your New Opportunity
External belief handling: address the final false belief that outside forces will block them even if the vehicle and they are fine

Worked Example — 'The 3 Secrets Of Funnel Hacking': Secret #1 Funnel Hacking (how to ethically study top funnels), Secret #2 Funnel Cloning (how to then clone their proven offer funnels in less than 10 minutes), Secret #3 My #1 Traffic Hack (how to get the same customers your competitors are currently going to)

Alternate worked example — 'The 3 Secrets' general template: Secret #1 'The 4 Stories You HAVE To Tell To Create A Table Rush', Secret #2 'How ONE Presentation Replaced 60+ Full Time Sales People', Secret #3 'How To Stand On Stages Without Leaving The Comfort Of Your Own Home'
exercises: Note the Fladlien quote on 'variety of different angles' and keep it as the design principle for the 3 Secrets
